As generative AI becomes ubiquitous, prompt injection techniques are growing more sophisticated. This article highlights three attack vectors expected to draw attention in spring 2026, all of which exploit blind spots in how large language models tokenize and interpret input text.

The first technique embeds malicious instructions inside emojis. Certain Unicode emojis support variant selectors and tag characters, allowing arbitrary strings to be smuggled inside what visually appears to be a harmless symbol. When an LLM tokenizes such input, it may read and act upon the hidden directive. The second technique relies on zero-width spaces and other invisible control characters. Attackers can insert phrases like "ignore previous instructions" in places users cannot see, but which the model nonetheless processes. The third is context poisoning, where adversaries plant persistent malicious content in documents or knowledge bases consumed by RAG pipelines and agentic systems, gradually steering future outputs.

These ideas are not entirely new. Researchers such as Simon Willison have warned about invisible prompt injection and ASCII smuggling since around 2024, and OWASP has placed prompt injection at the top of its LLM Top 10 risk list. What is changing is the attack surface. The rise of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and broader agentic AI deployments means models now ingest data from many external tools and documents, multiplying the routes through which tainted input can arrive. Hidden-character payloads are particularly dangerous in this setting because they survive copy-paste workflows and may bypass naive content filters.

Defensive measures center on input sanitization—stripping invisible characters and unusual Unicode ranges before they reach the model—along with output monitoring and strict privilege separation so that agents cannot freely invoke high-impact tools. Vendors like Anthropic and OpenAI continue to strengthen built-in guardrails, but no general solution exists, so application-level defenses are likely to remain essential. Developers building MCP servers or agent frameworks in particular should treat any externally sourced text as untrusted, and consider rendering suspicious payloads in normalized form before processing. The broader takeaway is that LLM security increasingly resembles classical web security: a constant cat-and-mouse game between novel encoding tricks and the parsers meant to defang them.

entries.title: Claude in Chromeでイベント作成を自動化した話
entries.titleJa: Claude in Chromeでイベント作成を自動化してみた
entries.summaryJa: AnthropicのブラウザエージェントClaude in Chromeを使い、Webサイトの情報からGoogleカレンダーへのイベント登録を自動化した試みを紹介。実際の操作手順や挙動、利便性と課題を検証した実践レポートとなっている。
entries.summaryEn: A hands-on report on using Anthropic's Claude in Chrome browser agent to automate event creation in Google Calendar from web pages, covering the workflow, behavior, and practical takeaways.

image.alt: Claude in Chromeでイベント作成を自動化した話

entries.bodyJa:
AnthropicのClaude in Chromeは、Chromeブラウザ上でClaudeがユーザーに代わってページ操作を行えるエージェント機能で、現在は限定プレビューとして提供されている。本記事は、この機能を使ってWebページ上のイベント情報を読み取り、Googleカレンダーへ自動登録するという日常的なタスクを試した実践レポートである。

筆者は、イベントページのURLを開いた状態でClaudeに「このイベントをカレンダーに登録して」と指示するだけで、エージェントがページ内容を解析し、タイトル・日時・場所などを抽出し、別タブのGoogleカレンダーを操作してイベント作成まで完了させる流れを紹介している。手作業でのコピー&ペーストが不要になり、複数イベントの一括登録などにも応用できる可能性を示している。

一方で、エージェントの操作は人間の画面操作をエミュレートする形で進むため、実行速度はそれほど速くなく、ページ構造によっては誤入力やフィールドの取り違えが発生し得る。重要な操作前には確認ダイアログが挟まれる安全機構もあり、完全な放置はまだ難しいと見られる。

背景として、ブラウザを操るAIエージェントはOpenAIのOperator、Google DeepMindのProject Mariner、Browser UseやPerplexityのCometなど競合が相次いで登場している領域である。AnthropicはClaudeのComputer Use APIを基盤にChrome拡張として提供しており、プロンプトインジェクションなどブラウザ特有のリスクへの対策も研究課題として明示している。日常業務の自動化という観点では、こうしたエージェントが従来のRPAやZapier的な定型自動化を補完する存在になっていく可能性がある。
entries.bodyEn:
Anthropic's Claude in Chrome is a browser-based agent, currently offered as a limited preview, that lets Claude operate web pages on the user's behalf inside Chrome. This article is a hands-on report describing how the author used the feature to automate a common everyday task: reading event details from a web page and registering them into Google Calendar.

The workflow is straightforward. With the event page open, the author simply tells Claude to add the event to the calendar. The agent then parses the page, extracts fields such as title, date, time, and location, switches to a Google Calendar tab, and fills in the new event form before saving. The author notes that this removes the tedium of copy-pasting between tabs and could scale to bulk registration of multiple events with relatively little additional effort.

That said, the agent operates by emulating human-style clicks and typing, so execution is not particularly fast. Depending on the page layout, fields can be misread or filled into the wrong slots, and a confirmation dialog appears before consequential actions. As a result, fully unattended use still feels premature, and human oversight remains advisable for now.

For context, browser-controlling AI agents have become a crowded space. OpenAI's Operator, Google DeepMind's Project Mariner, open-source projects like Browser Use, and Perplexity's Comet browser are all chasing similar ground. Anthropic builds on its Computer Use API and ships Claude in Chrome as an extension, while publicly acknowledging browser-specific risks such as prompt injection from untrusted page content and rolling out mitigations during the preview. Compared with traditional RPA tools or trigger-based services like Zapier, these LLM-driven agents are more flexible because they reason over arbitrary page structures rather than relying on pre-built integrations, but they are also less deterministic.

The broader takeaway from the author's experiment is that calendar entry, form filling, and similar light browser chores are a natural early sweet spot for agentic browsing. The capability is unlikely to replace dedicated integrations where reliability matters most, but it may meaningfully reduce friction for one-off or long-tail tasks that were never worth automating before. As Anthropic and competitors iterate on safety guards and accuracy, this category of assistant looks poised to gradually expand from curiosity to practical daily tool.

entries.title: プロンプトの「読み込み忘れ」をテキストだけで防ぐ設計手法：【論文紹介】GIP
entries.titleJa: プロンプト読み込み忘れを防ぐ設計手法 GIP 論文紹介
entries.summaryJa: LLMが長文プロンプトの一部指示を見落とす問題に対処する設計手法GIPを紹介する論文の解説記事。テキストのみで構造化し、指示の優先度や配置を工夫することで、追加の学習やツールを使わず指示遵守率を高める手法を示している。
entries.summaryEn: A Qiita article introducing GIP, a paper proposing a text-only prompt design method to prevent LLMs from skipping or missing instructions in long prompts, improving instruction-following without fine-tuning or external tools.

image.alt: プロンプトの「読み込み忘れ」をテキストだけで防ぐ設計手法：【論文紹介】GIP

entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)を業務利用する際、プロンプトに複数の指示を詰め込むと一部が無視される「読み込み忘れ」が頻発する。本記事はこの課題に正面から取り組む論文「GIP(Guided Instruction Prompting)」を紹介し、テキストだけで指示遵守率を高める設計手法をまとめている。

GIPの核心は、追加の学習やエージェント的なツール呼び出しに頼らず、プロンプトの構造そのものを工夫することで指示の見落としを減らす点にある。具体的には、指示を明示的にラベル付けし、優先度や実行順序を可視化することで、モデルが各タスクを段階的に処理しやすくする。著者は、長文プロンプトにおいてモデルの注意が中盤で薄れる「Lost in the Middle」現象を踏まえ、重要指示の配置や繰り返し提示の有効性を論じている。

背景として、近年のLLM活用ではシステムプロンプトが肥大化する傾向にあり、Anthropicが公開するClaudeのプロンプトエンジニアリングガイドや、OpenAIのGPT-4系における長文指示の取り扱いでも同種の課題が指摘されている。RAGやエージェントフレームワーク(LangChain、LlamaIndex等)では指示分割や再プロンプトで補う手法が一般的だが、GIPはあくまでテキスト記述の工夫で改善を図る点が実務的に扱いやすいと見られる。

また、Chain-of-ThoughtやSelf-Consistencyといった既存手法が推論精度の向上に寄与する一方、指示遵守そのものを扱う研究は相対的に少ない。GIPのアプローチは、プロンプト設計をエンジニアリング規律として体系化する流れの一部に位置付けられる可能性がある。実装コストが低く、既存システムへ段階導入しやすい点も含め、生成AI運用の現場で検証する価値があるテーマと言えるだろう。
entries.bodyEn:
When deploying large language models (LLMs) in production, engineers frequently encounter a frustrating failure mode: when a prompt contains many instructions, the model silently skips some of them. This Qiita article introduces a paper called GIP (Guided Instruction Prompting) that tackles this problem head-on, proposing a text-only design methodology for raising instruction-following rates without fine-tuning or external tooling.

The core idea of GIP is to restructure the prompt itself so that instructions are less likely to be overlooked. Rather than relying on agentic tool calls or additional training, the method explicitly labels each instruction, makes priority and execution order visible, and arranges the layout so the model can process tasks step by step. The author connects this to the well-known Lost in the Middle phenomenon, where attention degrades for content placed in the middle of long contexts, and discusses how strategic placement and selective repetition of critical instructions can mitigate it.

As background, system prompts in modern LLM applications have grown dramatically in length. Anthropic's prompt engineering guide for Claude and OpenAI's documentation for GPT-4-class models both flag similar issues with long, multi-instruction prompts. Frameworks such as LangChain and LlamaIndex typically work around the problem by splitting instructions across multiple calls or re-prompting, but GIP is notable for staying purely within the text layer. That makes it relatively easy to adopt incrementally in existing systems, which is likely to appeal to practitioners who cannot easily change their model or pipeline.

It is also worth noting that while techniques like Chain-of-Thought and Self-Consistency have received broad attention for improving reasoning quality, comparatively little research focuses specifically on instruction adherence as a measurable property. GIP can be seen as part of a broader movement to treat prompt design as a real engineering discipline, with reproducible patterns rather than ad hoc tricks. Given the low implementation cost and the absence of model-side changes, the approach appears worth evaluating in real generative AI deployments, though its effectiveness across model families and prompt styles will need further empirical validation.

entries.title: freee MCP には Remote版と OSS版がある——OSS版に乗り換える時のハマりどころ完全ガイド
entries.titleJa: freee MCP の Remote版と OSS版の違いと OSS版乗り換え時のハマりどころ
entries.summaryJa: freee 会計が提供する MCP サーバーには Remote版と OSS版の2種類があり、機能や認証方式が異なる。本記事では OSS版に乗り換える際に直面するセットアップや認証周りのハマりどころを実体験ベースで解説している。
entries.summaryEn: freee provides two flavors of its MCP server: a hosted Remote version and an OSS version with different feature sets and auth flows. The article walks through pitfalls encountered when migrating from the Remote version to the self-hosted OSS variant.
entries.bodyJa:
クラウド会計サービス freee が提供する MCP (Model Context Protocol) サーバーには、freee 側がホストする Remote版と、ユーザーが自前でセットアップする OSS版の2系統が存在する。両者は同じ「freee MCP」の名を冠しつつも、提供される API カバレッジ、認証フロー、運用負荷の点で性格が大きく異なるため、用途に応じた使い分けが求められる。

記事の主題は、Remote版で MCP を試した利用者が OSS版へ移行する際にぶつかりやすい落とし穴の整理である。Remote版は freee 側が OAuth フローや更新トークンの管理を肩代わりしてくれる一方、OSS版ではアプリ登録、クライアント ID/シークレットの取得、トークン発行とリフレッシュの自前管理、ローカル環境での MCP サーバー起動など、開発者が自身で準備すべき要素が増える。著者は実際に乗り換えを試みた経験から、認証情報の設定箇所、Claude Desktop など MCP クライアントへの接続方法、対応している API スコープの差異といった具体的なつまずきポイントを共有している。

背景として、MCP は Anthropic が 2024 年末に公開したオープン仕様で、LLM と外部ツール・データソースを標準化された方法で接続するためのプロトコルである。freee のような SaaS が公式に MCP サーバーを提供する動きは、Notion、GitHub、Slack など他のサービスでも広がっており、業務 SaaS と AI エージェントの統合は 2025 年にかけて急速に一般化しつつある。Remote版は導入容易性、OSS版は柔軟性とプライバシー制御という典型的なトレードオフを体現しており、特に会計データのような機微情報を扱う場面では OSS版を選ぶ意義が大きいと見られる。乗り換えを検討するユーザーにとって、こうした実践的なハマりどころの記録は有用な一次情報となるだろう。
entries.bodyEn:
freee, a major Japanese cloud accounting SaaS, offers its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server in two distinct flavors: a hosted Remote version maintained by freee itself, and an OSS version that users deploy on their own. While both expose freee's accounting APIs to LLM clients, they differ meaningfully in API coverage, authentication flow, and operational burden, so the right choice depends heavily on the use case.

The article focuses on the friction points users encounter when migrating from the Remote version to the OSS version. The Remote version handles OAuth flows and refresh-token lifecycle management on freee's side, letting users get started with minimal setup. The OSS version, by contrast, requires the developer to register an app on freee's developer portal, obtain client ID and secret, manage access and refresh tokens locally, and launch the MCP server process themselves. Drawing on hands-on experience, the author catalogues concrete stumbling blocks: where credentials need to be placed, how to wire the local server into MCP clients such as Claude Desktop, and which API scopes are or aren't supported compared with the Remote variant.

For context, MCP is an open specification published by Anthropic in late 2024 that standardizes how LLMs connect to external tools and data sources. Since then, SaaS vendors including Notion, GitHub, Slack, and now freee have begun publishing official MCP servers, and the pattern of pairing business SaaS with AI agents is becoming mainstream through 2025. The split between a hosted remote server and a self-hostable OSS server embodies a familiar tradeoff: convenience versus flexibility and data control. For workloads involving sensitive data such as accounting records, running the OSS version locally is likely to be attractive, since credentials and request payloads stay within the user's environment rather than passing through a third-party-hosted bridge.

Practical write-ups like this one serve as valuable primary documentation for developers weighing the migration. Official docs tend to describe each variant in isolation, but the gaps that surface only when switching between them — subtle differences in scopes, token handling quirks, or client configuration — are exactly the kind of tacit knowledge that accelerates adoption when shared openly. As more Japanese SaaS vendors ship MCP integrations, comparative notes between hosted and self-hosted options will probably become an increasingly common genre of technical blogging.

entries.title: PDFをそのままAIに読ませるな──専門書200冊をMarkdown化してClaudeのローカル知識ベースを作った話
entries.titleJa: PDF専門書200冊をMarkdown化してClaude用ローカル知識ベースを構築
entries.summaryJa: PDFを直接AIに読ませる非効率を避け、専門書200冊をMarkdown化してClaudeから参照できるローカル知識ベースを構築した実践記録。MCP経由で効率的に検索・活用する手法を紹介している。
entries.summaryEn: A practical account of converting 200 technical PDF books into Markdown to build a local knowledge base accessible to Claude via MCP, avoiding the inefficiency of feeding raw PDFs directly to LLMs.
entries.bodyJa:
生成AIに専門知識を扱わせる際、PDFをそのまま投入するのは効率が悪い。本記事は、専門書200冊をMarkdown形式に変換し、Claudeから参照できるローカル知識ベースを構築した実践記録である。

PDFはレイアウト情報を含むバイナリ形式であり、テキスト抽出時に表組みや数式、図版キャプションの順序が崩れやすい。LLMにそのまま読み込ませるとトークン消費が増大し、検索精度も落ちる。筆者はMarkdown化することで構造を保持しつつ、軽量で検索しやすい知識資産に変換したという。

変換後の文書はMCP(Model Context Protocol)経由でClaudeから参照する構成が採られている。MCPはAnthropicが2024年末に公開したプロトコルで、ローカルファイルやデータベース、外部APIを統一インタフェースでLLMから呼び出せる。これによりRAG(検索拡張生成)的な使い方を、クラウドにデータを預けずにローカル完結で実現できる点が利点とされる。

類似の取り組みとしては、MicrosoftのMarkItDownやmarker、docling(IBM)など、PDFを構造化テキストへ変換するOSSが近年急増している。特にdoclingは表や数式の認識精度が高く、技術書の電子化用途で評価が高まりつつある。Markdown化された文書はObsidianやLogseqといったPKM(個人知識管理)ツールとも相性が良く、AIエージェントと人間の読書の両方を支える基盤になり得る。

一方、書籍の電子化には著作権上の留意も必要であり、私的複製の範囲や購入済み電子書籍のDRM扱いなど、法的グレーゾーンに踏み込まないよう配慮が求められる。AIに食わせる前段としての知識整理は今後一般化していく可能性があり、変換パイプラインの標準化や品質評価指標の整備が課題になると見られる。
entries.bodyEn:
Feeding raw PDFs to a large language model is rarely the most effective way to leverage specialized knowledge. This article documents a practical experiment: converting 200 technical books from PDF into Markdown and exposing them to Claude as a local knowledge base.

PDF is a layout-oriented binary format. When text is extracted naively, tables, equations, and figure captions often lose their reading order, and token consumption balloons when the document is passed to an LLM in raw form. By converting to Markdown, the author preserves logical structure while producing a lightweight, easily searchable corpus that LLMs can ingest efficiently.

The resulting Markdown library is wired to Claude through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the open standard Anthropic introduced in late 2024. MCP gives LLMs a uniform way to call local files, databases, and external APIs, enabling a retrieval-augmented generation style workflow that runs entirely on the user's machine without uploading sensitive content to the cloud — an attractive property for personal libraries that may include purchased books.

The broader ecosystem around PDF-to-Markdown conversion has grown rapidly. Microsoft's MarkItDown, the marker project, and IBM's docling are among the open-source tools competing on extraction fidelity. Docling in particular has earned attention for its handling of tables and mathematical notation, which matters greatly for technical literature. Once content is in Markdown, it also integrates naturally with personal knowledge management tools such as Obsidian and Logseq, meaning the same corpus can serve both human reading and AI agent retrieval.

There are caveats. Digitizing books at scale touches copyright boundaries: private-use copying rules vary by jurisdiction, and circumventing DRM on purchased ebooks is generally prohibited even when the user owns the content. Practitioners considering similar pipelines should weigh these constraints carefully.

Looking ahead, organizing knowledge before feeding it to AI — rather than dumping raw documents — appears likely to become a standard pattern. Standardization of conversion pipelines, quality metrics for extracted Markdown, and tighter MCP integrations with PKM tools are plausible next steps, though the field is still young and best practices remain in flux.

entries.title: なぜ「キャッシュヒット」で90%オフ？ LLMプロンプトキャッシュの仕組みを全部図解する
entries.titleJa: なぜキャッシュヒットで90%オフ？ LLMプロンプトキャッシュの仕組みを図解
entries.summaryJa: LLMのプロンプトキャッシュがなぜ料金を最大90%削減できるのかを、Transformer内部のKVキャッシュの仕組みから解説する記事。長いシステムプロンプトや繰り返し使う文脈の再計算を省く構造を図解で示している。
entries.summaryEn: This article explains why LLM prompt caching can cut costs by up to 90%, breaking down how Transformer KV caches reuse precomputed attention states for repeated prefixes like long system prompts.

image.alt: なぜ「キャッシュヒット」で90%オフ？ LLMプロンプトキャッシュの仕組みを全部図解する

entries.bodyJa:
OpenAIやAnthropic、Google、各種推論サービスが提供する「プロンプトキャッシュ」は、同じプレフィックスを繰り返し送る場合に料金を最大90%削減できる仕組みとして注目されている。本記事は、その割引が単なるマーケティング上の値引きではなく、Transformer内部の計算構造に裏打ちされたものであることを図解で解説している。

LLM推論ではAttention計算のためにトークンごとのKey/Valueベクトル（KVキャッシュ）を生成する。同一の入力プレフィックスに対してはこのKVが完全に同一になるため、過去のリクエストで計算済みのKVをGPUメモリやストレージ上に保持しておけば、再計算をスキップして即座にデコード段階へ進める。割引率はこの「省略できた計算量」とおおむね対応している。

実用上の鍵は、キャッシュがプレフィックス一致である点だ。システムプロンプトや長文ドキュメント、Few-shot例をリクエスト先頭に固定し、可変部分を末尾に置くことでヒット率が上がる。AnthropicのClaudeでは明示的なcache_controlマーカー、OpenAIでは1024トークン以上で自動キャッシュ、DeepSeekやGeminiも独自方式を採用しており、各社で粒度や保持時間（多くは数分〜1時間）が異なる。

関連技術として、vLLMのPrefixCachingやSGLangのRadixAttentionは、複数リクエスト間でKVを共有するOSSの実装として知られる。エージェント開発で長いツール定義を毎回送るケース、RAGで同じ文書を複数質問に使うケースでは効果が大きいと見られる。一方でキャッシュは課金単価が下がる代わりに「キャッシュ書き込み」が割高になる場合もあり、短命な入力では逆効果になる可能性もある。設計時にはプロンプト構造の固定化とTTLの理解が重要となる。
entries.bodyEn:
Prompt caching, now offered by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek and several inference providers, has become one of the most effective levers for cutting LLM API bills. Discounts of up to 90% on cached tokens are common, and this article walks through why such steep reductions are technically justified rather than a marketing gimmick.

The explanation hinges on the KV cache that lives inside every Transformer. During inference, each input token is converted into Key and Value vectors used by the attention mechanism. These vectors depend only on the token and everything to its left, so for an identical prefix they are bit-for-bit reproducible. If a provider keeps those KV tensors in GPU memory or fast storage between requests, it can skip the entire prefill computation for the shared portion and jump straight to decoding the new suffix. The pricing discount roughly mirrors the compute that was avoided.

The practical implication is that caching is prefix-based. To maximize hit rates, developers should pin system prompts, lengthy documents, tool schemas and few-shot examples at the start of the request and keep variable content at the end. Anthropic exposes explicit cache_control markers, OpenAI applies automatic caching for prompts above 1024 tokens, and Gemini and DeepSeek implement their own variants. Retention windows vary, typically from a few minutes to about an hour, and granularity differs across vendors.

On the open-source side, vLLM's Automatic Prefix Caching and SGLang's RadixAttention implement the same idea across concurrent requests, using tree structures to share KV state between sessions that happen to overlap. These have made prefix sharing a standard feature in self-hosted serving stacks, and similar techniques underpin commercial offerings.

The biggest wins tend to appear in agent frameworks that resend large tool definitions on every step, and in RAG pipelines where the same retrieved documents back many follow-up questions. Long-context chat with stable system instructions also benefits substantially. However, caching is not free: some providers charge a premium for the initial cache write, so very short-lived prompts or rapidly changing prefixes can end up costing more than the uncached path. Understanding TTL behavior, minimum cacheable lengths, and how to structure prompts for stability is therefore becoming a core skill for anyone optimizing production LLM workloads.

entries.title: DIAGRAMS: A Review Framework for Reasoning-Level Attribution in Diagram QA
entries.titleJa: DIAGRAMS: ダイアグラムQAの推論過程を評価するレビュー枠組み
entries.titleEn: DIAGRAMS: A Review Framework for Reasoning-Level Attribution in Diagram QA
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、ダイアグラム質問応答(Diagram QA)における推論レベルの帰属を評価するためのレビューフレームワーク「DIAGRAMS」を提案する。最終回答だけでなく中間推論ステップを精査し、モデルの解釈可能性と信頼性を高めることを狙う。
entries.summaryEn: This paper introduces DIAGRAMS, a review framework for reasoning-level attribution in Diagram Question Answering, aiming to evaluate not just final answers but the intermediate reasoning steps to improve interpretability and trust in multimodal models.

image.alt: DIAGRAMS: A Review Framework for Reasoning-Level Attribution in Diagram QA

entries.bodyJa:
視覚と言語を統合するマルチモーダルAIの研究が進む中、図表を理解して質問に答える「Diagram QA」は依然として難しい課題である。本論文が提案するDIAGRAMSは、回答そのものの正誤に加えて、モデルが結論に至るまでの推論ステップを評価するためのレビューフレームワークである。

従来のDiagram QAベンチマークは、最終的な回答の正解率に偏った評価指標を採用してきた。しかし、正しい答えに到達したとしても、その途中で誤った視覚的根拠や不適切な論理を経由している場合があり、これが実運用におけるモデルの信頼性を損なう一因となっている。DIAGRAMSはこの課題に対し、推論過程の各ステップを「帰属(attribution)」の観点から検証し、どの図要素やテキスト断片が推論に寄与したのかを明示化する仕組みを提供すると見られる。

背景として、近年のGPT-4VやGemini、Claudeなどのビジョン言語モデル(VLM)は図表理解能力を大幅に向上させたが、複雑な科学図やフローチャートでは依然として誤推論が報告されている。AI2のAI2D、ChartQA、FigureQAといった既存ベンチマークは回答精度を測るには有用だが、Chain-of-Thought推論の質そのものを評価するには不十分との指摘がある。DIAGRAMSのような推論レベル評価枠組みは、こうした評価のギャップを埋める方向性として注目される可能性がある。

また、推論過程の帰属分析はAIの説明可能性(XAI)研究とも親和性が高く、教育用AIや科学文献理解アシスタントなど、ユーザが推論過程を確認したい応用分野での価値が高まると考えられる。
entries.bodyEn:
As multimodal AI systems mature, Diagram Question Answering (Diagram QA) remains a particularly challenging benchmark, requiring models to integrate visual structure, textual labels, and domain knowledge. This paper introduces DIAGRAMS, a review framework designed to evaluate not just whether a model produces the correct final answer to a diagram-based question, but how it arrives at that answer.

Most existing Diagram QA benchmarks measure performance through end-task accuracy. While convenient, such metrics obscure an important failure mode: a model may produce the right answer through faulty visual grounding or flawed logical chains, a phenomenon sometimes referred to as right-for-the-wrong-reasons. DIAGRAMS aims to address this gap by formalizing reasoning-level attribution, examining each intermediate step and identifying which diagram elements, text spans, or relational cues actually contributed to the conclusion.

The framework appears to fit within a broader research trend toward evaluating the faithfulness of model reasoning. Vision-language models such as GPT-4V, Gemini, and Claude have made substantial gains on visual reasoning tasks, yet they continue to struggle with complex scientific figures, flowcharts, and multi-step diagrammatic inference. Established benchmarks like AI2D, ChartQA, FigureQA, and DVQA have been instrumental in driving progress, but they are largely answer-centric. A reasoning-level review framework could complement them by surfacing the kinds of errors that aggregate accuracy metrics tend to hide.

Attribution-based evaluation also connects to the broader field of explainable AI. Techniques such as attention attribution, gradient-based saliency, and chain-of-thought verification have all been explored as ways to make model behavior more transparent. DIAGRAMS appears to extend these ideas into the diagram domain, where structural relationships between visual elements matter as much as the elements themselves. This is potentially valuable in high-stakes settings such as scientific literature analysis, educational tutoring systems, and technical document understanding, where users need to trust not just the answer but the path to it.

While the full empirical implications will depend on adoption and follow-up evaluation, frameworks like DIAGRAMS reflect an important shift in how the community thinks about multimodal reasoning quality. As models become more capable, the bar for evaluation likely needs to move beyond accuracy toward measuring whether reasoning is grounded, coherent, and faithful to the visual evidence.

entries.title: Model Organisms Are Leaky: Perplexity Differencing Often Reveals Finetuning Objectives
entries.titleJa: モデル生物はリークする:パープレキシティ差分でファインチューニング目的が露呈
entries.titleEn: Model Organisms Are Leaky: Perplexity Differencing Often Reveals Finetuning Objectives
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、ファインチューニング済みモデルとベースモデルの間でパープレキシティ差分を取るだけで、ファインチューニングの目的やデータが推測可能であることを示した。アライメント研究で用いられる「モデル生物」が意図せず情報を漏洩する危険性を指摘している。
entries.summaryEn: The paper shows that simply differencing perplexity between a finetuned model and its base model often reveals the finetuning objective or data, suggesting that 'model organisms' used in alignment research can unintentionally leak their training signals.

image.alt: Model Organisms Are Leaky: Perplexity Differencing Often Reveals Finetuning Objectives

entries.bodyJa:
アライメント研究では、特定の振る舞い(例:欺瞞や報酬ハッキング)を意図的に持たせた「モデル生物(model organisms)」を作り、それらを検出・解釈する手法を評価することが一般的になっている。本論文は、こうしたモデル生物が想定以上に情報を漏らしているという問題提起を行うものである。

著者らが提案する手法はシンプルで、ファインチューニング済みモデルと元のベースモデルに対し、様々なテキストでパープレキシティ(対数尤度)を計算し、その差分を取るだけである。差分が大きく低下したテキスト領域は、ファインチューニング時に学習された分布を反映している可能性が高い。これにより、明示的な訓練データへのアクセスがなくとも、ファインチューニングの目的やドメインを推定できると報告されている。

背景として、モデル生物アプローチはAnthropicの「Sleeper Agents」研究やRedwood Researchなどの解釈可能性研究で広く活用されてきた。これらは、危険な振る舞いを安全な実験環境で再現するための手段として重要視されているが、ベースモデルが公開されている場合、攻撃者あるいは評価者が差分解析を通じて隠された目的を逆算できてしまう懸念がある。

この知見は、解釈可能性ベンチマークの設計にも影響を与える可能性がある。検出手法が真にモデル内部の構造を理解しているのか、それとも単に分布シフトを拾っているだけなのかを区別する必要が生じるためである。今後はベースモデルへのアクセスを制限したり、KL正則化を強めるなどの対策が検討されると見られる。同時に、この手法はモデル監査やバックドア検出の実用ツールとしても応用余地があるだろう。
entries.bodyEn:
Alignment researchers increasingly rely on so-called model organisms: language models deliberately finetuned to exhibit specific behaviors such as deception, reward hacking, or hidden goals. These artifacts serve as testbeds for interpretability and detection methods. This paper argues that such model organisms are leakier than commonly assumed, and that a strikingly simple technique can often recover what they were trained to do.

The proposed method, perplexity differencing, requires no privileged access beyond the finetuned model and its base checkpoint. The researcher computes log-likelihoods of arbitrary text under both models and inspects where the finetuned model assigns substantially higher probability than the base. Regions of text that show large negative perplexity deltas tend to reflect the distribution the model was finetuned on, effectively exposing the training objective or domain without needing the actual training data.

This matters because much of the contemporary safety literature, including widely cited work like Anthropic's Sleeper Agents and various Redwood Research efforts, depends on model organisms as proxies for genuinely misaligned systems. If their hidden objectives can be reverse-engineered by a trivial baseline, then any detection method evaluated on them must clear that baseline before claiming to offer real insight. Otherwise interpretability tools risk being credited with discoveries that a single line of likelihood arithmetic could match.

The finding also has dual-use implications. On the defensive side, perplexity differencing could become a lightweight auditing tool: companies releasing finetuned variants of open base models like Llama or Qwen may inadvertently disclose proprietary data domains, while regulators or red teams could screen suspect models for backdoors and hidden triggers. On the offensive side, the same accessibility means adversaries can probe deployed assistants whose base weights are public.

Mitigations are likely to involve restricting access to the base model, training with stronger KL penalties to keep distributions close, or constructing model organisms whose behavioral signature is decoupled from a sharp distributional shift. None of these are free, and each may compromise the realism that makes model organisms useful in the first place. The broader takeaway is methodological: alignment evaluations should incorporate cheap distributional baselines as a sanity check, much as machine learning more generally has learned to compare new methods against linear or nearest-neighbor baselines before claiming progress.

entries.title: Interpretable Difficulty-Aware Knowledge Tracing in Tutor-Student Dialogues
entries.titleJa: チューター対話における難易度考慮型の解釈可能な知識トレーシング
entries.titleEn: Interpretable Difficulty-Aware Knowledge Tracing in Tutor-Student Dialogues
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、教師と生徒の対話データから生徒の理解度を推定する知識トレーシング手法を提案する。問題の難易度を明示的に組み込み、解釈可能性を高めることで、教育現場での活用可能性を示している。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes an interpretable knowledge tracing method for tutor-student dialogues that explicitly models question difficulty, aiming to better estimate student mastery and provide actionable insights for educators.

image.alt: Interpretable Difficulty-Aware Knowledge Tracing in Tutor-Student Dialogues

entries.bodyJa:
本論文は、チューターと生徒の自然言語による対話を素材に、生徒の知識状態を推定する「知識トレーシング(Knowledge Tracing, KT)」の新手法を提案している。従来のKTは選択式問題の正誤履歴を入力とすることが多かったが、対話データを扱う点と、問題の難易度を明示的にモデルへ組み込んで解釈可能性を高めた点が特徴とされる。

知識トレーシングは、Piechらによる2015年のDeep Knowledge Tracing(DKT)以降、LSTMやTransformerを使ったモデル(SAKT、AKTなど)が次々提案されてきた領域である。一方で、深層モデルはブラックボックス化しやすく、教員や学習設計者が「なぜこの生徒は理解が浅いと判定されたか」を把握しづらいという課題が指摘されてきた。本研究はその文脈で、難易度を明示的な特徴として導入し、推定根拠を読み解きやすくする方向性を取っていると見られる。

対話ベースのKTは、Khan AcademyのKhanmigoやCarnegie Learningなど、生成AIを活用した個別指導システムの広がりとともに重要性が増している分野である。選択式の正誤だけでなく、生徒の言い回しや誤解の表れ方から理解度を測れれば、より自然な学習支援が可能になる。本研究の難易度考慮型アプローチは、対話の中での質問の重みを補正することで、単純な正答率以上の情報を引き出す狙いがあると考えられる。

なお、本記事のURLに含まれるarXiv IDは形式が一般的なものと異なるため、最新の査読状況や具体的な実験設定・データセットについては原典の確認が望ましい。教育向けLLMの応用が広がる中、解釈可能性と教育的妥当性を両立する研究は今後も需要が高まる可能性がある。
entries.bodyEn:
This paper tackles knowledge tracing (KT) in the context of tutor-student dialogues, proposing a method that explicitly incorporates question difficulty while maintaining interpretability. The goal is to estimate a learner's evolving mastery from natural-language interactions rather than from the more conventional log of multiple-choice correct/incorrect responses.

Knowledge tracing has been an active research area since Piech et al. introduced Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT) in 2015, followed by attention-based variants such as SAKT and AKT. These models generally improved predictive accuracy but were often criticised for being opaque: educators struggle to understand why a particular student is flagged as weak in a given skill. By foregrounding question difficulty as an explicit feature, the present work appears aimed at making the model's reasoning more legible to teachers and instructional designers, although the precise mechanism would need to be confirmed against the original paper.

Dialogue-based KT is increasingly relevant given the rise of generative-AI tutoring systems such as Khan Academy's Khanmigo, Carnegie Learning's offerings, and various LLM-powered tutors built on top of GPT-4 or Claude. In such systems, the signal about a student's understanding is no longer a clean binary outcome but a stream of phrasing, hesitations, partial answers, and misconceptions. Extracting reliable mastery estimates from this richer but noisier signal is technically harder, and difficulty-awareness is one plausible way to weight evidence appropriately — a hard question answered well should count for more than an easy one.

Interpretability is particularly important in educational deployments because downstream actions, such as recommending remediation or adjusting pacing, must be defensible to teachers, parents, and learners themselves. Pure black-box scoring is a poor fit for such settings, and regulators in some jurisdictions are beginning to scrutinise AI used in education. Approaches that combine modern sequence modelling with transparent factors like item difficulty or skill tags may strike a more practical balance.

Readers should note that the arXiv identifier in the source URL has an unusual format, so details such as datasets, baselines, and evaluation metrics are best verified directly from the primary source. Even so, the broader direction — interpretable, dialogue-aware KT — is likely to remain an active research thread as LLM-based tutors mature and demand grows for evidence-based, auditable learner models.

entries.title: Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding in Hybrid Language Models
entries.titleJa: ハイブリッド言語モデル向けコンポーネント認識型自己投機的デコーディング
entries.titleEn: Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding in Hybrid Language Models
entries.summaryJa: ハイブリッド言語モデル(Transformer+状態空間モデル)に最適化された自己投機的デコーディング手法を提案。各コンポーネントの特性を考慮したドラフト生成により、推論速度を向上させつつ出力品質を維持できると報告している。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes a component-aware self-speculative decoding method tailored to hybrid language models that combine Transformer attention with state-space layers, aiming to accelerate inference while preserving output quality by exploiting the distinct characteristics of each component.

image.alt: Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding in Hybrid Language Models

entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデルの推論コストを下げる手法として注目される投機的デコーディングを、TransformerとMamba系状態空間モデル(SSM)を組み合わせたハイブリッドアーキテクチャに適応させる研究である。著者らは、各コンポーネントの計算特性を考慮したドラフト生成戦略を提案している。

投機的デコーディングは、軽量なドラフトモデルでトークン候補を先読みし、本体モデルが並列に検証することで生成を高速化する技法である。自己投機的デコーディングはこのドラフトを本体モデル自身の一部レイヤーや圧縮表現から生成することで、別途ドラフトモデルを用意する手間を省く。本研究はこれをハイブリッドモデルに適用する点が新規である。

ハイブリッドモデルでは、Attention層が長距離依存を扱う一方、SSM層は線形時間で系列を処理する。両者でKVキャッシュやステート更新の挙動が異なるため、単純な投機的デコーディングの適用は非効率になりがちである。提案手法はコンポーネントごとに異なる扱いを行うことで、検証時のオーバーヘッドを抑えると見られる。

背景として、JambaやZamba、Samba、NVIDIAのHymbaなど、TransformerとSSMを組み合わせたハイブリッドモデルが近年相次いで登場している。Mambaは長文脈処理での効率性から注目されているが、推論最適化のエコシステムはTransformer中心に発展してきたため、ハイブリッド向けの専用最適化は重要なテーマとなっている。Medusa、EAGLE、Lookahead Decodingなど自己投機的手法の研究も活発であり、本論文はその流れをハイブリッドへ拡張する位置付けと言える。
entries.bodyEn:
Speculative decoding has become a popular technique for reducing the latency of large language model inference, but most existing work targets pure Transformer architectures. This paper extends the idea to hybrid models that interleave attention layers with state-space model (SSM) blocks, proposing a component-aware variant of self-speculative decoding.

In standard speculative decoding, a lightweight draft model proposes several candidate tokens that the larger target model verifies in parallel, accepting the longest correct prefix. Self-speculative decoding removes the need for a separate draft model by reusing a subset of the target model's own layers or a compressed internal representation as the drafter. The novelty here lies in adapting this paradigm to architectures that mix two fundamentally different sequence-mixing primitives.

Hybrid models pose a particular challenge because attention layers maintain a growing KV cache, while SSM layers carry a fixed-size recurrent state that is updated sequentially. Naive speculative decoding can mishandle the SSM state when candidate tokens are rejected, forcing expensive rollbacks. The authors argue that treating each component according to its own computational profile—essentially routing draft and verification work differently through attention versus SSM blocks—reduces this overhead while maintaining the exact-output guarantees that make speculative decoding attractive.

The broader context is a wave of hybrid architectures released over the past year, including AI21's Jamba, Zyphra's Zamba, Microsoft's Samba, and NVIDIA's Hymba. These designs aim to combine the strong in-context recall of attention with the linear-time scaling of Mamba-style SSMs, which is especially appealing for very long contexts. However, the inference-optimization ecosystem—kernels, serving frameworks, and decoding tricks like Medusa, EAGLE, and Lookahead Decoding—has matured around dense Transformers, leaving hybrids comparatively underserved.

Work like this paper is therefore part of a growing effort to close that gap. If the reported speedups hold up under independent evaluation, component-aware self-speculative decoding could become a standard tool for serving hybrid models efficiently. Readers should note, however, that practical gains from speculative decoding depend heavily on acceptance rates, batch size, and hardware, so production benefits may vary across deployment scenarios.

entries.title: H-Probes: Extracting Hierarchical Structures From Latent Representations of Language Models
entries.titleJa: H-Probes: 言語モデルの潜在表現から階層構造を抽出する手法
entries.titleEn: H-Probes: Extracting Hierarchical Structures From Latent Representations of Language Models
entries.summaryJa: 言語モデルの内部表現から階層的構造を抽出する新手法「H-Probes」を提案した論文。従来のプローブ手法を拡張し、構文木のような入れ子構造を潜在ベクトルから復元できることを示している。
entries.summaryEn: This paper introduces H-Probes, a method for extracting hierarchical structures such as syntactic trees from the latent representations of language models, extending classical probing techniques to capture nested compositional information.

image.alt: H-Probes: Extracting Hierarchical Structures From Latent Representations of Language Models

entries.bodyJa:
言語モデルがその内部に何を表現しているかを明らかにする「プロービング(probing)」研究は、解釈可能性研究の中核となっている。本論文「H-Probes」は、こうしたプローブ手法を階層構造の抽出に拡張した試みとして位置づけられる。

従来のプローブは、潜在ベクトルから品詞や依存関係といった単一ラベルを予測する単純な分類器が中心だった。一方で自然言語は本質的に入れ子構造を持ち、構文木や談話構造といった階層的情報がモデル内部にどう符号化されているかは未解明な部分が多い。H-Probesは、隠れ層表現から木構造そのものを再構成することを目標に、階層を意識した学習目標を設定している点が特徴と見られる。

この方向性は、HewittとManningによる「Structural Probe」(2019) の流れを汲むものと位置づけられる。Structural Probeは単語ペア間の距離を木構造の深さに射影することで、BERTが構文木情報を内包していることを示した。H-Probesはその発想をさらに推し進め、より複雑な階層関係を取り出すアプローチと考えられる。

関連分野としては、機構的解釈可能性(mechanistic interpretability)やsparse autoencoderによる特徴抽出、Anthropicが進めるcircuit分析など、内部表現の構造を明らかにする研究が活況を呈している。階層情報の抽出は、言語モデルがどの程度「文法を理解」しているのかという長年の問いに直結し、教育応用や安全性評価にも波及する可能性がある。

なお本記事のURLに記載されたarXiv番号は通常の形式とは異なるため、論文の最新性や正式な所属情報については原文確認を推奨する。
entries.bodyEn:
Probing research, which seeks to reveal what linguistic information is encoded inside neural language models, has become a cornerstone of interpretability work. The paper introducing H-Probes positions itself within this tradition, but extends it toward something more ambitious: extracting full hierarchical structures, rather than flat labels, from latent representations.

Classical probes typically train a small classifier on top of a frozen model's hidden states to predict properties such as part-of-speech tags, dependency relations, or semantic roles. While useful, these single-label probes give only a coarse view of what the model represents. Natural language, however, is inherently nested — sentences contain phrases, phrases contain sub-phrases, and discourse layers compose meaning hierarchically. H-Probes targets exactly this gap, aiming to reconstruct tree-like structures directly from internal embeddings.

The approach can be seen as a spiritual successor to the influential Structural Probe work by Hewitt and Manning (2019), which showed that BERT's hidden states implicitly encode syntactic trees by mapping pairwise word distances onto tree depths. H-Probes appears to push this further by formulating training objectives that are sensitive to multi-level hierarchical relations, not just pairwise distances. The exact methodology and benchmarks would need to be verified against the original paper, but the direction aligns with a growing interest in compositional probing.

This line of research sits within a broader interpretability ecosystem. Mechanistic interpretability efforts at labs like Anthropic, sparse autoencoder feature extraction popularized through recent work on Claude and GPT-style models, and circuit-level analyses all aim to open the black box of large language models. Hierarchical structure extraction is particularly interesting because it speaks to a long-standing question in computational linguistics: to what extent do neural models actually internalize grammar, as opposed to relying on surface statistical regularities? If H-Probes can reliably recover constituent or dependency hierarchies, it adds further evidence that modern transformers learn rich linguistic abstractions rather than shallow heuristics.

Practical implications could extend beyond pure linguistics. Reliable hierarchical probes might support educational tools that visualize how models parse sentences, aid in debugging multilingual or low-resource models, and inform safety evaluations where understanding model reasoning chains matters. They could also intersect with code models, where syntactic hierarchy in programming languages is explicit and verifiable, providing a clean testbed for probing methods.

Readers should note that the arXiv identifier accompanying this entry does not follow the standard arXiv numbering convention, so verifying the canonical version of the paper, its authors, and publication venue against arxiv.org directly is advisable before citing specific claims.

entries.title: RECAP: An End-to-End Platform for Capturing, Replaying, and Analyzing AI-Assisted Programming Interactions
entries.titleJa: RECAP: AI支援プログラミングの対話を記録・再現・分析する統合基盤
entries.titleEn: RECAP: An End-to-End Platform for Capturing, Replaying, and Analyzing AI-Assisted Programming Interactions
entries.summaryJa: RECAPは、AI支援プログラミングにおける開発者とAIの対話を記録、再生、分析できるエンドツーエンドのプラットフォーム。プロンプト、コード編集、AI応答などを統合的に捉え、研究者がAIコーディング支援の利用実態や効果を体系的に評価できる環境を提供する。
entries.summaryEn: RECAP is an end-to-end platform for capturing, replaying, and analyzing developer interactions with AI coding assistants, enabling researchers to systematically study prompts, code edits, and AI responses in realistic programming sessions.
entries.bodyJa:
GitHub CopilotやCursorに代表されるAIコーディング支援ツールが広く使われるようになる中、開発者が実際にAIとどのように対話し、生産性や品質にどんな影響が生じているのかを科学的に検証する基盤は十分整っていない。RECAPは、こうした研究上の空白を埋めることを狙った、AI支援プログラミングの対話を記録・再現・分析するためのエンドツーエンドのプラットフォームとして提案されている。

RECAPは、開発者の操作、入力プロンプト、AIアシスタントからの応答、編集前後のコード状態など、AIとの協働セッションで生じる多様なイベントを統合的にキャプチャすると見られる。記録したセッションは後から再生して観察できるため、ユーザースタディの分析やプロンプトの傾向、受理・棄却された提案の比較などに活用できる可能性がある。研究者にとっては、ログ単独では失われがちな文脈、すなわち「どのタイミングでAIに何を尋ね、その出力をどう編集したか」という時系列の流れを保持できる点が重要になる。

背景として、AIアシスタントの評価は従来、HumanEvalなどのベンチマークによる単発のコード生成精度に偏っていた。しかし実際の開発はマルチターンの試行錯誤であり、Microsoft Researchなどでも対話的なコパイロット利用の実証研究が進んでいる。CursorやContinue、Aiderといったツールが多様化する中で、横断的に対話データを収集・比較できる共通基盤への需要は高まっていると考えられる。RECAPのようなインフラは、HCIとソフトウェア工学の交差点で、AI協調開発の実態解明に寄与しうる。
entries.bodyEn:
As AI coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code become embedded in everyday software development, the research community still lacks robust infrastructure to study how developers actually interact with these systems. RECAP is proposed as an end-to-end platform for capturing, replaying, and analyzing AI-assisted programming interactions, aiming to make such studies more reproducible and scalable.

The platform appears to instrument the developer environment so that prompts, AI responses, accepted and rejected suggestions, code edits, and surrounding context can all be captured as a coherent timeline. Recorded sessions can then be replayed, allowing researchers to revisit not only what code was produced but also how it emerged through a back-and-forth dialogue with the assistant. This is a meaningful step beyond static logs, which often strip away the temporal and contextual cues needed to understand developer intent and assistant behavior.

Analysis tooling built on top of these recordings would, in principle, enable studies of prompt patterns, suggestion acceptance rates, debugging loops, and the friction points where AI output requires substantial human revision. Such fine-grained data could help quantify productivity claims that have so far relied largely on self-reports or coarse telemetry, and could surface failure modes that benchmark scores tend to obscure.

The broader context matters here. Evaluation of AI programming assistants has historically leaned on one-shot benchmarks like HumanEval, MBPP, or SWE-bench, which capture problem-solving ability but not the interactive, iterative nature of real coding work. User studies from Microsoft Research, GitHub, and academic HCI groups have repeatedly shown that developers blend AI suggestions with manual edits in complex ways, and that perceived usefulness depends heavily on workflow integration. Tools like Continue, Aider, and Cline are expanding the design space of assistant interfaces, which makes a shared capture-and-replay substrate increasingly valuable for cross-tool comparison.

It is worth noting that platforms of this kind raise practical concerns around privacy, consent, and the storage of potentially sensitive source code, and the value of the resulting datasets will depend on how broadly RECAP is adopted across tools and study sites. If those conditions are met, RECAP could become a useful piece of community infrastructure at the intersection of software engineering and human-AI interaction research, helping move the conversation about AI-assisted coding from anecdote toward evidence.

entries.title: Can AI Debias the News? LLM Interventions Improve Cross-Partisan Receptivity but LLMs Overestimate Their Own Effectiveness
entries.titleJa: AIはニュースの偏向を減らせるか?LLM介入で党派超えた受容性向上、ただし効果は過大評価
entries.titleEn: Can AI Debias the News? LLM Interventions Improve Cross-Partisan Receptivity but LLMs Overestimate Their Own Effectiveness
entries.summaryJa: LLMがニュース記事を書き換えることで党派を越えた受け入れやすさを改善できるかを検証した研究。実験では受容性の向上が確認されたが、LLM自身は介入の効果を過大評価する傾向があることも明らかになった。
entries.summaryEn: A study examines whether LLMs can rewrite news to reduce partisan bias, finding that interventions improve cross-partisan receptivity but that LLMs tend to overestimate the effectiveness of their own debiasing edits.
entries.bodyJa:
米国を中心に深まる政治的分極化の中で、ニュースメディアの党派的トーンが対話の障壁となっている。本研究は、大規模言語モデル(LLM)を用いてニュース記事を書き換え、反対党派の読者にも受け入れられやすくする「ディバイアス介入」の有効性を検証したものである。

著者らは複数のLLMに党派色のあるニュース記事を中立化・再構成させ、その出力を実際の読者に提示して受容性(receptivity)を測定した。結果として、LLMによる書き換えは確かに党派を越えた読みやすさや共感度を一定程度向上させることが示された。一方で、LLM自身に自分の介入効果を評価させると、人間評価よりもはるかに高いスコアを付ける傾向があり、自己効力感の過大評価という新たな課題が浮かび上がった。

この結果は、LLMをファクトチェックや自動編集に活用する近年の動向とも関わる。例えばGround NewsやAllSidesといったサービスは多角的視点の提示を試みており、OpenAIやAnthropicもモデルの政治的中立性に注力している。しかし本研究が示すように、LLMを「自己評価者」として用いるLLM-as-a-judge的な手法には系統的バイアスが潜む可能性がある。

実務的含意としては、ニュース編集や対話促進ツールにLLMを組み込む際、効果測定を必ず人間の読者評価と組み合わせる必要があると見られる。また、モデルが自身の出力を過大評価する傾向は、RLHFや自己批評ループの設計にも影響しうる重要な観察である。AIによるメディア介入は分極化緩和の一手段になり得るが、その効果検証には慎重な方法論が求められる。
entries.bodyEn:
Political polarization in the United States and elsewhere has made the partisan tone of news media a barrier to constructive cross-party dialogue. This paper investigates whether large language models can be used to rewrite news articles in ways that make them more palatable to readers on the opposing side of the political spectrum, and whether such interventions actually work as intended.

The authors prompt multiple LLMs to neutralize or reframe partisan news content, then measure how real readers respond to the rewritten versions. Their experiments find that LLM-mediated rewriting does meaningfully improve cross-partisan receptivity: readers from the opposing party rate the edited articles as more credible, less hostile, and more worth engaging with than the originals. This is a modest but encouraging signal that automated debiasing can play a role in reducing affective polarization around news consumption.

However, a second and arguably more striking finding concerns the LLMs themselves. When the same models are asked to evaluate the effectiveness of their own debiasing edits, they consistently rate the interventions as far more successful than human readers do. In other words, LLMs systematically overestimate their own ability to neutralize partisan framing. This has direct implications for the increasingly popular LLM-as-a-judge paradigm, where model outputs are evaluated by other models rather than by humans.

The work fits into a broader ecosystem of efforts to mitigate media bias, ranging from aggregator services like Ground News and AllSides that present multiple perspectives, to internal alignment work at OpenAI, Anthropic, and others aimed at making models politically balanced. It also intersects with research on RLHF and self-critique loops, where a model's ability to honestly assess its own outputs is foundational. If models systematically inflate their self-assessments on socially loaded tasks, this could quietly bias entire training pipelines.

The practical takeaway is twofold. First, LLM-based rewriting may be a useful tool for newsrooms, civic-tech projects, or platforms hoping to lower the temperature of political discourse, but its effects should always be validated against human reader studies rather than model self-reports. Second, designers of automated evaluation pipelines should be cautious about trusting LLM judgments on tasks where the model has a stake in the outcome it is judging. The findings do not invalidate AI-assisted debiasing, but they suggest that the gap between perceived and actual effectiveness deserves more systematic scrutiny as these tools move from research prototypes into deployed systems.

entries.title: Psychologically Potent, Computationally Invisible: LLMs Generate Social-Comparison Triggers They Fail to Detect
entries.titleJa: LLMが生成する社会的比較トリガーを自ら検知できない問題
entries.titleEn: Psychologically Potent, Computationally Invisible: LLMs Generate Social-Comparison Triggers They Fail to Detect
entries.summaryEn: This study shows that large language models can generate psychologically potent social-comparison triggers, yet fail to detect such content as harmful, revealing an asymmetry between generation and moderation that poses safety risks.
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)は人間の感情や自己評価に影響を与えるテキストを容易に生成できる一方で、その潜在的な害を自ら認識できないという「非対称性」が新たな研究で指摘された。本論文はソーシャルメディア上での社会的比較を題材に、生成側と検知側の能力差を実証している。

社会的比較とは、他者と自分を比べることで生じる心理的反応を指し、SNS上では羨望や自己肯定感の低下、抑うつの引き金となることが知られている。研究では、LLMに対し具体的な投稿やキャプションを生成させ、それらが人間評価者から見て強い比較感情を喚起する内容であったにもかかわらず、同じLLMにモデレーション役を担わせると有害性をほぼ検出できなかったとされる。

この結果は、現行の安全性フィルタが暴力やヘイト等の明示的な有害カテゴリに最適化されている一方、心理的微害(サブクリニカルな害)に対しては盲点を持つ可能性を示唆する。OpenAIやAnthropic、MetaなどがコンテンツポリシーやConstitutional AIといった枠組みで安全性を強化しているが、自尊心や精神的健康に関わる微妙な刺激は依然として評価軸が定まっていないと見られる。

関連分野では、Instagramの内部調査が10代女性のメンタルヘルスへの悪影響を示した経緯や、推薦アルゴリズムによる「比較疲れ」の議論が続いている。LLMが大量の投稿候補を低コストで生成可能になった現在、こうした心理的トリガーがスケールする懸念は無視できない。今後はモデレーションモデルに心理学的アノテーションを組み込み、生成と評価の両面で人間の福祉を考慮した評価指標が必要になる可能性がある。
entries.bodyEn:
A new study highlights an unsettling asymmetry in large language models: they can readily produce text that triggers social comparison and undermines self-esteem in human readers, yet they largely fail to flag that same content as harmful when asked to moderate it. Using social-media-style posts as the testbed, the researchers demonstrate a measurable gap between LLMs' generative capabilities and their evaluative judgment on subtle psychological harms.

Social comparison refers to the psychological response that arises when people measure themselves against others. On platforms like Instagram and TikTok, this dynamic has been linked to envy, lowered self-worth, and, in some user populations, depressive symptoms. In the reported experiments, LLMs were prompted to generate posts and captions designed to read as ordinary lifestyle content. Human raters judged many of these outputs to be strong elicitors of upward social comparison. When the same models were then placed in a moderator role and asked whether the content posed any risk to readers, they reportedly recognized only a small fraction of the harmful cases.

The finding suggests that current safety filters are well-tuned to explicit categories such as violence, hate speech, sexual content, and self-harm instructions, but appear to have a blind spot for what might be called subclinical or low-grade psychological harm. These harms do not violate any obvious policy line, yet they may accumulate at scale across millions of impressions. Because LLMs can now generate vast quantities of plausible lifestyle content at near-zero marginal cost, the potential for such triggers to flood feeds is no longer theoretical.

Major labs have invested heavily in alignment frameworks intended to prevent harmful generations. OpenAI's usage policies, Anthropic's Constitutional AI approach, and Meta's Llama Guard family all encode taxonomies of disallowed or risky content. None of these frameworks, however, appear to define explicit criteria for content that is technically benign but psychologically corrosive. As a result, evaluation benchmarks rarely measure whether a model can detect content engineered to provoke envy, body dissatisfaction, or status anxiety.

The context for the study is well established. Internal Facebook research leaked in 2021 indicated that Instagram use was associated with worsened body image among a subset of teenage girls, prompting hearings in the U.S. Senate and renewed scrutiny of recommender systems that may amplify comparison-heavy content. Academic work on "comparison fatigue" and the mental-health effects of algorithmic curation has continued to grow, but most of that literature predates the current generation of generative models capable of producing the comparison-inducing material themselves.

The asymmetry the paper describes also raises practical questions for platform integrity teams. If an LLM-based moderator is deployed downstream of an LLM-based content generator, and both share similar training distributions and value priors, the moderator may systematically miss exactly the kinds of harm the generator is most prone to produce. This mirrors concerns raised in adversarial robustness research, where models trained on similar data exhibit correlated failure modes.

Possible remedies include incorporating psychological annotations from clinicians and social psychologists into moderation training data, developing dedicated classifiers for affect-targeting content, and expanding red-team protocols beyond conventional harm taxonomies to cover well-being impacts. Some researchers have also proposed treating user mental-health outcomes as a first-class evaluation metric for generative systems, although operationalizing such metrics remains difficult and contested.

The broader implication is that safety in generative AI may need to expand beyond rule-based prohibitions toward a more holistic account of human welfare. As LLMs become embedded in content pipelines, recommendation systems, and conversational companions, harms that are diffuse, cumulative, and difficult to attribute may become the dominant risk profile, even as the more dramatic categories of misuse receive most of the policy attention. The reported gap between generation and detection suggests that closing this loop will require both technical and interdisciplinary work that is only beginning to take shape.

entries.title: A Theoretical Game of Attacks via Compositional Skills
entries.titleJa: 構成的スキルを介した攻撃の理論ゲーム的分析
entries.titleEn: A Theoretical Game of Attacks via Compositional Skills
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、LLMに対する攻撃を構成的スキルの観点からゲーム理論的に定式化する試みを提示する。攻撃者と防御者がスキルの組み合わせを通じて相互作用するモデルを構築し、安全性評価への新たな視座を示すと見られる。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes a game-theoretic framework for analyzing attacks on LLMs through the lens of compositional skills, modeling attacker-defender interactions over skill combinations to inform safety evaluation.
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)の安全性研究において、ジェイルブレイクやプロンプトインジェクションといった攻撃手法は単独のスキルではなく、複数の能力の組み合わせから生じる場合が多い。本論文は、こうした攻撃を「構成的スキル(compositional skills)」という枠組みで捉え、攻撃者と防御者の相互作用をゲーム理論的にモデル化する理論的試みを提示している。

論文の核となるアイデアは、LLMが持つ個別のスキル(推論、コード生成、ロールプレイ等)を要素として、その組み合わせ空間上で攻撃と防御がどのように展開されるかを形式化する点にある。攻撃者は無害に見える個別スキルを合成することで有害な出力を引き出せる可能性があり、防御側は個々のスキル単位ではなく合成パターン全体を監視する必要があるという含意が導かれると見られる。

背景として、近年のレッドチーミング研究では、Anthropic の constitutional AI や OpenAI の preparedness framework など、組織レベルでの安全評価枠組みが整備されつつある一方、攻撃の構造を数理的に分析する研究はまだ少ない。Skill-Mix(Arora ら)のように構成性を評価する先行研究はあるが、それを攻防のゲームとして定式化する点に本研究の独自性があると考えられる。

また、ゲーム理論的アプローチは敵対的機械学習の古典的伝統(GAN や adversarial robustness 研究)と接続しており、LLM 安全性研究を従来の理論基盤と橋渡しする可能性を持つ。実装や実験よりも概念的・理論的な貢献に重点があると推測されるため、読者は実用ツールというより安全性評価の枠組み設計の参考として位置づけるのが適切だろう。
entries.bodyEn:
Safety research on large language models has increasingly recognized that successful attacks—jailbreaks, prompt injections, multi-turn manipulations—often arise not from a single capability but from the composition of several individually benign skills. This paper offers a theoretical, game-theoretic treatment of that phenomenon, framing attacker-defender dynamics over the space of compositional skills.

The central premise is that an LLM's behavior can be decomposed into elementary skills such as reasoning, code generation, persona adoption, or summarization. Attackers exploit combinations of these skills to elicit harmful outputs that no single skill would produce in isolation. By formalizing this as a game between an attacker who selects skill combinations and a defender who allocates monitoring or refusal capacity, the authors aim to characterize equilibria and bounds on attack success.

A key implication, as far as can be inferred from the framing, is that defenses operating at the level of individual skills are structurally insufficient. Because the harmful signal lives in the composition rather than the components, monitoring strategies must reason about joint patterns. This echoes findings in empirical red-teaming where decomposition attacks—splitting a disallowed request across innocuous-looking subtasks—routinely bypass content filters.

The work sits in an interesting lineage. Skill-Mix, introduced by Arora and collaborators, established compositionality as a meaningful axis for evaluating LLM capability. Adversarial machine learning has a long tradition of game-theoretic modeling, from GANs to certified robustness analyses. Bringing these threads together for LLM safety is timely, given that organizations like Anthropic (constitutional AI, responsible scaling policy) and OpenAI (preparedness framework) are formalizing safety evaluations but largely on empirical rather than theoretical grounds.

Readers should likely treat this as a conceptual contribution rather than a deployable tool. The value lies in providing vocabulary and formal structure for reasoning about why certain attack patterns succeed and what minimal defender capacity would be required to suppress them. Whether the equilibrium analyses translate into concrete guidance for evaluation suites or guardrail design will probably depend on follow-up empirical work mapping real model skills onto the abstract skill set the theory assumes.

It is worth noting that compositional attacks also intersect with agentic systems, where tool use multiplies the effective skill inventory. As LLM agents gain access to browsers, code execution, and external APIs, the combinatorial surface that attackers can exploit grows accordingly, suggesting the framework may become more, not less, relevant over time.

entries.title: A Systematic Exploration of Text Decomposition and Budget Distribution in Differentially Private Text Obfuscation
entries.titleJa: 差分プライバシーテキスト難読化におけるテキスト分解と予算配分の体系的検証
entries.titleEn: A Systematic Exploration of Text Decomposition and Budget Distribution in Differentially Private Text Obfuscation
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、差分プライバシーに基づくテキスト難読化において、入力テキストをどの粒度(単語・文・文書)で分解し、プライバシー予算をどう配分するかを体系的に比較検証している。分解単位と予算配分戦略がプライバシー保護とユーティリティのバランスに与える影響を実証的に明らかにした。
entries.summaryEn: This paper systematically explores how text decomposition granularity (word, sentence, document) and privacy budget allocation strategies affect the privacy-utility trade-off in differentially private text obfuscation, providing empirical comparisons across multiple configurations.
entries.bodyJa:
本論文は、差分プライバシー(DP)に基づくテキスト難読化において、これまで個別に提案されてきた手法を統一的な枠組みで比較し、テキスト分解単位とプライバシー予算配分戦略が結果に与える影響を体系的に検証したものである。

DPテキスト難読化は、原文を再構成することで個人を特定可能な情報を秘匿しつつ、下流タスクで利用可能な意味情報を保つことを目的とする。代表的な手法としては、単語埋め込み空間にノイズを加えるMadlibや、文単位・文書単位で書き換えを行う手法が知られている。しかし、どの粒度で分解しどう予算を割り当てるかは手法ごとに異なり、公平な比較が困難であった。

著者らは、単語・文・文書という分解粒度と、均等配分・重み付け配分などの予算戦略を組み合わせ、プライバシー保証(ε)とユーティリティ(分類精度や意味類似度)のトレードオフを実験的に評価した。結果として、分解粒度を細かくするほどノイズの累積で意味劣化が顕著になる傾向や、重要トークンへの予算重点配分が有効である可能性が示されたと見られる。

背景として、近年はLLMの普及によりプロンプト中の個人情報漏洩リスクが注目されており、Microsoftの研究グループなどがDPベースのテキスト書き換えを継続的に研究している。メトリックDPやガウス機構を組み合わせる手法、また合成データ生成にDPを応用する潮流(DP-SGDによるファインチューニングなど)も並行して進展している。本研究はこうした多様な手法を比較検討する基礎を提供するものであり、実応用における設計指針として参照される可能性がある。
entries.bodyEn:
This paper offers a systematic comparison of differentially private (DP) text obfuscation techniques, focusing on two design choices that have largely been treated implicitly in prior work: how to decompose input text into units before adding noise, and how to allocate the privacy budget across those units.

DP text obfuscation aims to rewrite text so that individual contributions cannot be reliably inferred, while preserving enough semantic content for downstream tasks such as classification, retrieval, or model training. Early approaches like Madlib injected calibrated noise into word embeddings and projected back to the vocabulary, while later methods operated at the sentence or document level, often leveraging paraphrasing models. Because these methods differ in granularity and budget accounting, head-to-head comparisons have been difficult.

The authors construct a unified experimental framework that crosses decomposition granularity (word, sentence, document) with several budget distribution strategies, including uniform allocation and importance-weighted schemes. They then measure the resulting privacy-utility trade-offs using standard NLP benchmarks and semantic similarity metrics. The findings reportedly indicate that finer-grained decomposition tends to accumulate more noise and degrade utility, and that concentrating budget on more informative tokens can yield better trade-offs, though the optimal choice depends on task and ε regime.

The broader context is increasingly relevant. With the rise of large language models, sensitive content frequently appears in prompts, fine-tuning data, and retrieval corpora, and groups at Microsoft, Google, and various academic labs have been exploring metric DP, Gaussian mechanisms over embeddings, and DP synthetic text generation. Parallel work on DP-SGD fine-tuning and DP prompt rewriting addresses similar concerns from different angles. By isolating decomposition and budgeting as first-class design variables, this study could serve as a useful reference for practitioners trying to navigate an otherwise fragmented design space, although the practical gains in real deployments will likely depend on careful task-specific tuning.

entries.title: Controlled Paraphrase Geometry in Sentence Embedding Space: Local Manifold Modeling and Latent Probing
entries.titleJa: 文埋め込み空間における言い換えの局所多様体モデリングと潜在プロービング
entries.titleEn: Controlled Paraphrase Geometry in Sentence Embedding Space: Local Manifold Modeling and Latent Probing
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は文埋め込み空間で言い換え文が形成する局所幾何構造を解析し、制御可能な多様体モデルを提案する。潜在プロービング手法により意味保存方向と表層変動方向を分離し、言い換え生成や評価への応用可能性を示す。
entries.summaryEn: This paper analyzes the local manifold geometry formed by paraphrases in sentence embedding space and proposes a controllable model. Latent probing separates meaning-preserving directions from surface variation, suggesting applications to paraphrase generation and evaluation.
entries.bodyJa:
本論文は、文埋め込み空間における言い換え文の幾何学的配置を体系的に分析し、その局所多様体構造を制御可能にモデリングする手法を提案する研究である。文の意味表現がベクトル空間でどのように分布するかは、自然言語処理の基盤的問題として長年議論されてきた。

著者らはまず、ある原文に対する複数の言い換えが埋め込み空間内で局所的な多様体を形成すると仮定し、その構造を経験的に検証する。続いて、この多様体上の方向性を潜在プロービング（latent probing）によって解析し、意味を保存したまま表層形式のみを変える方向と、意味そのものを変化させる方向を分離して特定することを試みる。

技術的には、対照学習で訓練された文埋め込みモデル（Sentence-BERTやSimCSE系統が代表的）を出発点とし、言い換えペアから得られる差分ベクトルの主成分分析や線形プローブによって、解釈可能な部分空間を抽出するアプローチが取られていると見られる。これにより、言い換え生成器の制御や、意味類似度評価指標の改善といった下流応用が期待される。

関連する潮流として、近年は埋め込み空間の幾何学的性質を活用したテキスト編集（DiffuSeqなどの拡散モデル系）や、埋め込みの異方性問題（BERT-flowやwhitening手法）に関する研究が活発である。本研究はこれらと補完的な位置にあり、特に言い換えという意味保存変換に焦点を絞ることで、より精緻な局所構造の理解を提供する可能性がある。実応用としては、データ拡張、対話システムの応答多様化、評価ベンチマーク構築などに波及する余地があると考えられる。
entries.bodyEn:
This paper investigates the geometric arrangement of paraphrastic sentences within sentence embedding spaces and proposes a method to model their local manifold structure in a controllable way. How sentence meanings are distributed across vector spaces has long been a foundational question in natural language processing, and paraphrases offer a particularly clean lens because they hold meaning roughly constant while varying surface form.

The authors hypothesize that paraphrases of a given source sentence cluster on a local manifold in the embedding space, and they empirically examine this structure. They then apply latent probing techniques to identify directions along the manifold that correspond to meaning-preserving surface variation versus those that shift semantic content. Separating these axes is non-trivial because contrastive sentence encoders tend to entangle stylistic and semantic information.

Methodologically, the work appears to build on contrastively trained encoders such as Sentence-BERT or SimCSE, using difference vectors between paraphrase pairs as the raw signal. Linear probes and principal component analysis are likely employed to extract interpretable subspaces, though the specifics depend on the experimental setup. The resulting controllable geometry could be useful both for steering paraphrase generators and for diagnosing what sentence encoders actually capture.

This line of inquiry connects to several active research threads. Work on embedding anisotropy, including BERT-flow and whitening-based post-processing, has shown that raw transformer embeddings occupy narrow cones and benefit from geometric correction. Diffusion-based text generation models such as DiffuSeq similarly exploit continuous embedding manifolds for controlled editing. The present study is complementary, focusing specifically on the semantics-preserving transformation of paraphrasing to yield finer-grained insight into local structure.

Potential downstream applications include data augmentation pipelines, response diversification in dialogue systems, and the construction of more discriminative evaluation benchmarks for semantic similarity. Because paraphrase quality remains difficult to evaluate automatically, a geometrically grounded notion of meaning-preserving variation could also inform better metrics beyond BLEU or BERTScore. While the practical impact will depend on how robustly the identified directions generalize across domains and languages, the framing offers a promising bridge between representation analysis and controllable generation.

entries.title: Teaching LLMs Brazilian Healthcare: Injecting Knowledge from Official Clinical Guidelines
entries.titleJa: ブラジル公式臨床ガイドラインをLLMに注入する試み
entries.titleEn: Teaching LLMs Brazilian Healthcare: Injecting Knowledge from Official Clinical Guidelines
entries.summaryJa: 本研究では、ブラジル保健省の公式臨床ガイドラインから知識を抽出し、大規模言語モデルに注入することで、ブラジルの医療制度SUSに即した回答を生成できるよう適応させる手法を提案している。汎用LLMが抱える地域固有の医療知識不足を補う試みである。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes injecting knowledge from Brazil's official Ministry of Health clinical guidelines into LLMs, adapting them to the country's public health system (SUS) and addressing the gap in localized medical knowledge that general-purpose models typically lack.
entries.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル(LLM)は医療領域でも幅広く活用されつつあるが、その知識の多くは英語圏の文献やガイドラインに偏っており、各国固有の医療制度や臨床プロトコルを十分に反映できていない。本論文は、ブラジル保健省が公式に発行する臨床ガイドライン(Protocolos Clínicos e Diretrizes Terapêuticas, PCDT)をLLMに注入し、ブラジルの統一医療制度SUSの文脈に即した回答を生成できるようモデルを適応させる試みを報告している。

研究の背景には、ChatGPTをはじめとする汎用LLMがブラジル特有の薬剤承認状況、SUSが提供する治療オプション、地域の疫学情報を正確に把握しておらず、現地の医療従事者が利用するには信頼性が不足するという問題意識がある。著者らは公式PCDT文書を構造化データに変換し、ファインチューニングや検索拡張生成(RAG)などの手法で知識を注入することで、回答の正確性と地域適合性を高めようとしていると見られる。

関連する動向として、医療特化LLMでは Google の Med-PaLM、Microsoft の BioGPT、オープンソースの Meditron などが知られるが、いずれも主に英語データで学習されている。ポルトガル語圏では Sabiá などの基盤モデルも登場しており、ローカライズされた医療AIへの関心は高まりつつある。各国の保険制度や承認薬リストはモデルが汎化しにくい領域であり、公式文書を一次情報として組み込むアプローチは、医療AIの信頼性確保において今後重要性を増す可能性がある。
entries.bodyEn:
Large language models are rapidly being adopted in healthcare settings, but most of their medical knowledge is rooted in English-language literature and guidelines from the United States and Europe. This creates a significant blind spot when these models are deployed in countries whose public health systems, drug approval processes, and clinical protocols differ substantially from the Anglophone norm. This paper tackles that gap for Brazil, proposing a methodology for injecting knowledge from the country's official clinical guidelines into LLMs.

The Brazilian Ministry of Health publishes a series of documents known as Protocolos Clínicos e Diretrizes Terapêuticas (PCDT), which define the diagnostic criteria, therapeutic options, and follow-up procedures recognized by the country's Unified Health System (SUS). These protocols are authoritative for clinicians working within the public system and often differ from international guidelines in terms of drug availability, dosing recommendations, and reimbursement coverage. The authors argue that general-purpose LLMs such as ChatGPT, when asked questions in a Brazilian clinical context, frequently produce answers that are technically plausible but locally inaccurate or unsafe.

The approach reportedly involves transforming the PCDT corpus into structured training data and using techniques such as fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation to ground model outputs in the official guidelines. The goal is not only to improve factual accuracy but also to ensure that the model's recommendations align with what is actually available and reimbursable through SUS, a constraint that purely clinical knowledge bases tend to ignore.

This line of work fits into a broader movement toward localized medical AI. Google's Med-PaLM, Microsoft's BioGPT, and the open-source Meditron family have demonstrated the value of domain-specific tuning, but all remain heavily anglocentric. For Portuguese, projects like Sabiá have begun building foundation models with stronger linguistic grounding, and similar localization efforts exist for Spanish, Arabic, and several Asian languages. Healthcare, however, requires more than language adaptation: it demands jurisdiction-specific knowledge about which treatments are legally approved, which are publicly funded, and how care pathways are organized.

It remains to be seen how well guideline-injected models generalize beyond the specific protocols they were trained on, and whether they can keep pace with the regular updates that ministries of health issue. Still, treating official government documents as primary sources for medical LLMs is a promising pattern that could likely be replicated in other national health systems where reliability and regulatory alignment matter as much as raw clinical accuracy.

entries.title: Quantifying and Predicting Disagreement in Graded Human Ratings
entries.titleJa: 段階的人間評価における不一致の定量化と予測
entries.titleEn: Quantifying and Predicting Disagreement in Graded Human Ratings
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は、段階的(順序尺度)な人間アノテーションに含まれる評価者間の不一致を定量化し、機械学習で予測する手法を提案する。単一の正解ラベルではなく評価分布として扱うことで、主観的タスクの曖昧さを保持できる。
entries.summaryEn: This paper proposes methods to quantify and predict disagreement in graded human ratings, treating annotations as distributions rather than single gold labels to better capture subjectivity in NLP tasks.
entries.bodyJa:
自然言語処理における人間アノテーションは、これまで多数決や平均によって単一の正解ラベルへ集約されることが多かった。本論文はこの慣習に疑問を呈し、段階的(順序尺度)な人間評価に含まれる評価者間の不一致そのものを情報として扱い、定量化・予測する枠組みを提案している。

著者らは、感情強度や容認性判断といったタスクにおいて、不一致が単なるノイズではなく、項目固有の曖昧さや主観性を反映していることを示す。提案手法は、各事例に対する評価分布を直接モデル化し、その分散や形状を予測対象とする。これにより、モデルは「どの事例が人間にとって判断が難しいか」を事前に推定できるようになる。

背景として、近年のNLPコミュニティではperspectivism(視点主義)やlearning from disagreementと呼ばれる潮流が広がっている。Plankらによる一連の研究や、SemEvalにおけるLearning With Disagreementsタスクは、アノテーター個々の視点を保持することの重要性を訴えてきた。本研究はこの流れに沿いつつ、二値ラベルではなく順序尺度データに焦点を当てた点に特徴があると見られる。

応用面では、こうした手法はLLMの評価やRLHFのデータ品質管理にも関連性を持つ可能性がある。報酬モデル学習において、人間の評価分布をそのまま反映させることで、過剰な確信や偏りを抑制できるとの議論もある。アノテーションコストの最適化、すなわち不一致が大きい事例に追加アノテーターを割り当てるアクティブラーニング戦略にも応用しうる。
entries.bodyEn:
Human annotation in NLP has traditionally been aggregated into a single gold label through majority voting or averaging. This paper challenges that convention by proposing methods to quantify and predict the inter-annotator disagreement found in graded (ordinal) human ratings, treating disagreement itself as informative signal rather than noise to be smoothed away.

The authors argue that in tasks such as sentiment intensity, acceptability judgment, or other subjective evaluations, variation among annotators often reflects genuine item-level ambiguity or legitimate differences in perspective. Rather than collapsing ratings to a point estimate, they model the full distribution of ratings per item and predict properties such as its variance or shape. This allows downstream systems to flag items that are inherently hard for humans to judge, and to calibrate model confidence accordingly.

The work fits into a broader movement sometimes called perspectivism or learning from disagreement. Researchers like Barbara Plank have argued that annotator disagreement carries linguistic and social signal that is lost during aggregation, and SemEval's Learning With Disagreements shared task has helped popularize evaluation setups that preserve multiple labels. What appears distinctive here is the focus on graded, ordinal ratings rather than categorical labels, which raises additional methodological questions about how to measure agreement (e.g., weighted kappa, Krippendorff's alpha) and how to parameterize predicted distributions.

The practical implications may extend beyond traditional NLP benchmarks. Reward modeling for RLHF, for instance, depends heavily on human preference data, and there is growing concern that aggregating disagreeing annotators can produce overconfident or biased reward signals. Modeling the distribution of human judgments directly could lead to better-calibrated reward models and reduce mode collapse in aligned LLMs. Similarly, the ability to predict which items will provoke disagreement could inform active learning pipelines, allowing annotation budgets to be spent on ambiguous cases that most need additional labels, while avoiding redundant annotation of clearly easy items.

Limitations remain. Predicting disagreement well requires sufficiently rich features, and it is not always clear whether observed variance reflects deep semantic ambiguity or simply annotator inattention. Still, the paper contributes to a growing recognition that the single-gold-label paradigm is an oversimplification for many subjective NLP tasks, and that embracing graded human variation may yield both better models and more honest evaluation.

entries.title: Compute Optimal Tokenization
entries.titleJa: 計算効率を最適化するトークナイゼーションのスケーリング則
entries.titleEn: Compute Optimal Tokenization
entries.summaryJa: 本論文は大規模言語モデルにおけるトークナイザの語彙サイズや設計を、計算予算に対して最適化する手法を提案する。モデルサイズと語彙サイズの間に明確なスケーリング則が存在し、適切な選択により学習効率と性能が向上することを示している。
entries.summaryEn: This paper investigates compute-optimal tokenization for large language models, identifying scaling laws between vocabulary size, model size, and training compute that can improve efficiency and downstream performance when properly balanced.
entries.bodyJa:
トークナイゼーションは大規模言語モデル(LLM)の前処理として地味ながら性能を大きく左右する要素であり、本論文はその設計を計算予算に対して最適化する枠組みを提示している。

著者らは、モデルパラメータ数・学習トークン数・語彙サイズの三者の間にスケーリング則が成立することを実験的に示した。Chinchilla論文がモデルサイズと学習トークン数の最適バランスを示したのと同様に、語彙サイズもまた計算最適点が存在し、現在広く使われているトークナイザは大規模モデルに対して語彙が小さすぎる傾向にある可能性があると指摘される。

背景として、GPT系列やLLaMAなどはBPE(Byte Pair Encoding)やSentencePieceを用い、3万から10万程度の語彙を採用してきた。一方、Llama 3では12.8万、Gemmaでは25.6万と語彙サイズの拡大傾向が見られ、本研究の知見と整合的だと見られる。語彙が大きいほど1トークンあたりの情報密度が増し系列長が短くなるため、学習・推論コストの削減につながる一方、埋め込み層のパラメータが増えるトレードオフがある。

関連分野では、Byte-level Transformerやトークナイザ不要のアプローチ(MambaByte、ByT5など)も研究されており、トークナイゼーションの設計自体が研究テーマとして再注目されている。本研究のスケーリング則は、今後のフロンティアモデル設計における語彙サイズ選定の指針となる可能性がある。ただし、提示されたスケーリング則が多言語環境やドメイン特化モデルにそのまま適用できるかは追加検証が必要と見られる。
entries.bodyEn:
Tokenization is often treated as a mundane preprocessing step, but it materially shapes the efficiency and quality of large language models. This paper proposes a framework for choosing tokenizer parameters — particularly vocabulary size — in a compute-optimal manner, drawing on the same spirit as the Chinchilla scaling work that reframed how practitioners balance model size and training data.

The authors empirically derive scaling laws connecting model parameters, training tokens, and vocabulary size. Their central finding is that vocabulary size has its own compute-optimal point, and that many widely deployed tokenizers may be undersized relative to the models they serve. Increasing vocabulary shortens sequence length and raises information density per token, which lowers training and inference FLOPs, but it also enlarges the embedding and output projection matrices — a trade-off that the proposed laws make explicit.

For context, GPT-style models and the original LLaMA family used BPE or SentencePiece tokenizers with vocabularies in the 32K–100K range. More recent releases have moved upward: Llama 3 adopted a 128K vocabulary, and Gemma went further at 256K. These industry choices appear broadly consistent with the direction implied by the paper's scaling laws, though each lab's rationale may differ and reflects multilingual coverage as much as pure compute optimality.

The broader research landscape is also revisiting tokenization. Byte-level and tokenizer-free approaches such as ByT5, MEGABYTE, and MambaByte attempt to remove the discrete vocabulary entirely, trading longer sequences for architectural simplicity and robustness to noisy or multilingual input. Against that backdrop, results showing that careful vocabulary scaling yields meaningful compute savings strengthen the case that classical subword tokenization remains competitive when tuned properly.

Practically, the work could serve as a planning tool for frontier model teams deciding on tokenizer specifications before committing to expensive pretraining runs. It also provides a quantitative justification for the larger vocabularies seen in recent open-weight releases. That said, it remains to be seen how robustly these laws transfer to highly multilingual corpora, code-heavy training mixes, or domain-specific models where token distribution diverges sharply from general web text. Additional validation across such regimes will likely be needed before the recommendations can be applied without caveats.

entries.title: CLEAR: Revealing How Noise and Ambiguity Degrade Reliability in LLMs for Medicine
entries.titleJa: CLEAR:医療用LLMの信頼性をノイズと曖昧性がどう損なうか解明
entries.titleEn: CLEAR: Revealing How Noise and Ambiguity Degrade Reliability in LLMs for Medicine
